title: The operation names of the rwb-payment proceeds and vendor-fee read, the rwb-case case-move answer and the rwb-source-data account and sale data product are not published
source: 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1.md (slides 19, 20, 41, 43); _work/msr/plan/ownership.json; Recovery Workbench TSD S5 Assets and auction v2 (T-A.1)
section: s3 Preconditions; s12.2 REST operations consumed; s12.8 Contract fakes; s13 Solution plan
description: The application story consumes four rows across three owners and no source document publishes the operation name of any of them. Architecture v5 slide 19 gives rwb-asset the consumed event ProceedsMatched but names no proceeds read and no case-move operation; the Ownership Map carries the four S5 rows only; TSD S5 T-A.1 lists this service's own operations and no neighbour's. The story therefore builds against a documented use and a placeholder, not a path.
evidence: Architecture v5 slide 19 IN lists JudgmentRecorded, AuctionResult, ProceedsMatched and PartnerResultSubmitted for rwb-asset and names no REST operation of P3, P8 or P1; slide 41 gives rwb-asset ownership of assets, holding, floor price, listings and auction rounds and names no proceeds read; the Ownership Map API rows for S5 are GET /assets, GET /assets/{assetId}, POST /assets/{assetId}/listings and POST /listings/{listingId}/rounds only.
owner_role: P3 rwb-case owner, P8 rwb-payment owner, P1 rwb-source-data owner
proposed: Each owner publishes the operation name of its row before the wave 3 tag, and RWB-S5-E4030-CON replaces the placeholder with the published name in a minor version.

title: No source names the table and column that hold the residual and its D9 hand-off, and the vendor-fee match is not assigned to a service
source: Recovery Workbench TSD S5 Assets and auction v2 (T3.1 tables, T3.2 lists, T3.3 relationships); Recovery Workbench FSD S5 Assets and auction v3 (A2.21); _work/msr/plan/ownership.json; legacy RWB-E4-030 Data table
section: s4 Flow steps 9 and 10; s8 BR3, BR5; s11 Data; s13 Configuration and reference data
description: Legacy AC2 raises the residual for the D9 decision and legacy AC3 matches the vendor fee, but neither the TSD S5 T3.1 tables nor the FSD A2.21 names a column for the residual or a table for its hand-off, and no source assigns the vendor-fee match to this service or to rwb-payment. The story writes the sale outcome on asset_sale and records the residual against the same row where a column exists, and it reads the vendor-fee match as rwb-payment's fact because the fee and its posting sit with the money; both readings are assumptions and neither is a value invented here.
evidence: TSD S5 T3.1 lists the asset and sale tables and names no shortfall or residual table; the legacy Data table lists proceeds under DF-FIN-001 to DF-FIN-009 and no residual entity; FSD S5 A2.21 states the outcome without naming the store; the Ownership Map gives proceeds to P8 and asset_sale to S5 with no residual row.
owner_role: S5 rwb-asset owner with P8 rwb-payment owner; P3 rwb-case owner for the D9 routing
proposed: The S5 data owner confirms the residual column on asset_sale or names the rwb-writeoff store, and the P8 owner confirms the vendor-fee match as its own fact; the DB story of the service adds the column in its own Flyway sequence if it does not exist.

title: The split plan carries no requirement id for this slice
source: _work/msr/plan (story and requirement rows); Recovery Workbench FSD S5 Assets and auction v3 (A2.21, FEAT-AST-21); Recovery Workbench Business Requirements Program v4
section: s2 Business rationale; s18 Traceability requirement table
description: The story serves FEAT-AST-21 of the FSD module S5, and the split plan's requirement rows carry no id for this slice, so the traceability table states the requirement by its feature and cites this gap instead of an invented REQ id.
evidence: The plan's requirement rows for rwb-asset do not include a row for the proceeds and shortfall slice; the FSD S5 A2.21 names FEAT-AST-21 without a REQ id in this slice's scope.
proposed: The requirement owner allocates a REQ id for the slice at the next plan revision and the traceability row is repointed without a story change.

title: No source names a published operation for the proceeds and shortfall step itself, and no element is defined for the residual in the contract
source: _work/msr/plan/ownership.json (S5 API rows); 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1.md (slides 19, 41); Recovery Workbench TSD S5 Assets and auction v2 (T-A.1)
section: CON s7 C4; s9 In review; s11 Data; s12.1 REST operations provided; s12.2; s12.7
description: The contract baseline must declare the surface of the step, and the only S5 operations the Ownership Map publishes are the four asset and listing rows. No source names an operation that exposes the proceeds and shortfall step, and no source defines a contract element for the residual. The baseline declares the two asset reads that answer the screens, declares the step's own operation as None with this gap, and declares the residual element only when its owner names the column.
evidence: The Ownership Map API rows for S5 are GET /assets, GET /assets/{assetId}, POST /assets/{assetId}/listings and POST /listings/{listingId}/rounds; TSD S5 T-A.1 names no proceeds operation; Architecture v5 slide 19 gives rwb-asset an inbound event and two outbound events and no operation for the step.
proposed: The service owner confirms at the tag whether the step exposes any operation; if it does, this baseline adds it in a minor version with its rights and its error set.

title: The split plan carries no requirement id for the contract slice and the Ownership Map table list omits the asset row
source: _work/msr/plan (story and requirement rows); _work/msr/plan/ownership.json (table rows); 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1.md (slides 19, 41); Recovery Workbench TSD S5 Assets and auction v2 (T3.1)
section: CON s3 Preconditions; s11 Data; s18 Traceability requirement table
description: Two documentation gaps meet in the contract slice. The plan's requirement rows carry no id for this slice, so the traceability table cites the feature and this gap. The Ownership Map table list gives asset_sale and listing to S5 and omits asset, which slides 19 and 41 and TSD S5 T3.1 read as S5; the baseline names asset as S5 on that reading and records it here rather than in an invented row.
evidence: The plan's requirement rows carry no row for the proceeds and shortfall slice; the Ownership Map table rows list asset_sale and listing under S5 and carry no asset row; Architecture v5 slide 41 and TSD S5 T3.1 treat the asset record as rwb-asset's.
owner_role: Program requirements owner and the Ownership Map maintainer
proposed: The requirement owner allocates a REQ id at the next plan revision and the Ownership Map adds the asset row to S5's table list; neither change alters a story shape.

title: RWB-S5-E4031-APP: the RAMC transfer step has no source for its call names, its pool, price and approval references, its timer or its screen owner
source: Template and Rules v1 R5.4, R5.5, R7.3 and R9; split_plan.json slices RWB-S5-E4031-APP and -CON (H, C, I, X); Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 19, 41, 43 and 44; Temporal and Drools Design Text Extract v1 slides 13, 14 and 28; Ownership Map v1 rows asset_sale, listing, asset, recovery_case, assignment, approval, rule_row, partner_instruction and template; Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 rows R-DIS-23, R-DIS-59 and R-DIS-60; TSD S5 Assets and auction v2 T2, T3.1, T3.2, T3.3, T4, T6.1 and T-A.1; FSD S5 Assets and auction v3 A2.22; legacy RWB-E4-031
description: (1) No source publishes the element names or the acceptance and refusal codes of the rwb-partner issueInstruction activity, and no source publishes the name of the rwb-case case-move answer; Architecture v5 slide 19 OUT gives the activity name only. (2) The transfer record has no table of its own and no column for the pool, the transfer-price template version or the committee-approval reference: asset_sale is the sale table of TSD S5 T3.1 (DF-SAL-009 to DF-SAL-019) and the Ownership Map table list has neither a RAMC transfer table nor a pool table, although LOV-SALE-CHANNEL carries the RAMC value. (3) Architecture v5 slide 19 OUT gives Decision: child: approval and the Ownership Map gives approval to P7, but no source says whether the committee approval is the P7 ApprovalWorkflow, what it decides or whether a REST approval operation exists. (4) The R-DIS-59 timer cell reads per agreement and no source gives it a duration or a unit, while the rule row and its timer specification are governed in rwb-decision. (5) PRT-06 Transfer confirmation has states but no named owner, and SCR-21 is a Workbench screen behind gateway-bff while the partner portal is served with rwb-partner. (6) The plan gives H of three rows and C, I and X empty, although the step also consumes rwb-partner, rwb-case, rwb-decision and rwb-source-data rows.
evidence: Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 row R-DIS-59 with Timer cell per agreement and Systems cell Partner Portal, Calculation Service; Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 rows R-DIS-23 (route = RAMC and committee approved, to ROUTE_APPROVED_RAMC) and R-DIS-60 (TRANSFER_COMPLETED to ASSET_TRANSFERRED); Architecture v5 slide 19 OUT line TMP Partner: issueInstruction (auction vendor) · Decision: child: approval; Architecture v5 slide 43 rows 22 and AssetSold; Ownership Map v1 api rows POST /cases/{caseId}/instructions and GET /partner/instructions with owner S9; Ownership Map v1 tables approval, rule_row and decision_log_entry owner P7, partner_instruction owner S9, template owner P6; TSD S5 v2 T3.1 asset_sale DF-SAL-009 to DF-SAL-019 with no pool, price-version or approval column and T3.2 LOV-SALE-CHANNEL with the value RAMC; FSD S5 v3 A2.22.3.2 field catalog and A2.22.4.4 no background event; split_plan.json slice RWB-S5-E4031-APP with H of three rows and C, I, X empty
area: Contract, data model, approval boundary, timer and screens
proposed: Read the defaults recorded in ASM-B-S5-05-E4031-1, keep them in the RWB-S5-E4031-CON baseline, and confirm the partner, case and approval names with S9, P3 and P7 before the baseline is tagged; raise the missing transfer table and the three missing columns to the Ownership Map owner if the reading is not accepted

title: RWB-S5-E4031-APP: the legacy endpoints name an S1 operation and a later S5 pricing operation, neither of which the transfer step calls
source: legacy RWB-E4-031 Endpoints and Permission checks tables; TSD S5 Assets and auction v2 T-A.1 and T6.1; Ownership Map v1 api rows POST /assets/{assetId}/valuations and POST /assets/{assetId}/listings with their rulings ASM-A6-api-6 and ASM-A6-api-15; FSD S5 Assets and auction v3 A2.22.3.3
description: The legacy Endpoints table lists POST /assets/{assetId}/valuations (API-S5-003, now rwb-valuation's under the Ownership Map ruling ASM-A6-api-6) and POST /assets/{assetId}/listings (API-S5-004, the pricing story's) with the right Asset and disposal C, and the legacy Permission checks table grants C for them. The transfer of a pool to RAMC calls neither operation, and the two operations this step does provide are the reads behind PRT-06 and SCR-21, which TSD S5 T-A.1 gives right R. The legacy rows therefore describe a surface this story does not own, and no source says which operation the C right of the feature attaches to.
evidence: legacy RWB-E4-031 Endpoints table rows POST /api/recovery/v1/assets/{assetId}/valuations and POST /api/recovery/v1/assets/{assetId}/listings with access Asset and disposal C; legacy RWB-E4-031 Permission checks table with right C; TSD S5 v2 T-A.1 rows API-S5-001 and API-S5-002 with right R and API-S5-003 to API-S5-005 with rights C and U; Ownership Map v1 api rows POST /assets/{assetId}/valuations owner S1 (ruling ASM-A6-api-6) and POST /assets/{assetId}/listings owner S5 (ruling ASM-A6-api-15); FSD S5 v3 A2.22.3.3 roles Sale officer primary and Head of NPA, RAMC user also uses
proposed: Name the two legacy endpoints in the story as operations of their owners that are not built here, declare only the two reads as provided with right R, and grant no C right to this step

title: RWB-S5-E4031-APP: the split plan and TSD S5 T8 carry no requirement id for FEAT-AST-22
source: split_plan.json slice RWB-S5-E4031-APP reqs; legacy_index.json RWB-E4-031 reqs; TSD S5 Assets and auction v2 T8 requirement traceability; FSD S5 Assets and auction v3 A2.22.1 and the Requirements served table

TSD S5 T8 maps REQ-S5-001 to REQ-S5-005 to FEAT-AST-01 and REQ-S5-006 to REQ-S5-010 to FEAT-AST-08, so no requirement row names FEAT-AST-22 Transfer a pool to RAMC or the joint venture. The story therefore traces to the feature, to FSD S5 A2.22 and to the legacy key, and the requirement table of section 18 carries the placeholder rather than an invented id.

title: RWB-S5-E4031-CON: the transfer element, the instruction element and the four consumed rows have no published names or fields
source: TSD S5 Assets and auction v2 T3.1, T3.2, T3.3 and T-A.1; Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 19, 43 and 45; Temporal and Drools Design Text Extract v1 slides 13 and 27; Ownership Map v1 rows asset_sale, listing, asset, recovery_case, approval, partner_instruction and the api row POST /cases/{caseId}/instructions; split_plan.json slice RWB-S5-E4031-CON
description: (1) The pool reference, the transfer-price template version and the committee-approval reference have no column in TSD S5 T3.1, so their property names, types and required flags are unstated and the contract can only declare them as identifiers with the placeholder. (2) The issueInstruction element and its acceptance and refusal codes are unnamed in every source. (3) The case-move answer, the element names of the approval answer and the operation name of the rwb-source-data read are unnamed, so three of the four consumed rows carry the placeholder. (4) No source publishes a REST approval operation, so the approval can only be declared as the answer of the P7 child workflow. (5) The service owns a topic but the step publishes nothing, so the contract must declare an absence that a reader may otherwise read as an omission.
evidence: TSD S5 v2 T3.1 asset_sale DF-SAL-009 to DF-SAL-019 and listing DF-SAL-001 to DF-SAL-008 with no pool, price-version or approval column; TSD S5 v2 T-A.1 with the two read operations only; Architecture v5 slide 19 OUT with the partner activity, the approval child and the two events; Ownership Map v1 api row POST /cases/{caseId}/instructions owner S9 with no element names; split_plan.json slice RWB-S5-E4031-CON with H, C, I and X empty
proposed: Declare the three references as identifiers with the placeholder, keep the four consumed rows with their placeholders and the partner path on the consumed side, declare no approval operation and no event, and tag the baseline when S9, P3 and P7 confirm the names

title: RWB-S5-E4031-CON: the instruction is both a partner REST path and a Temporal activity, and no source reconciles the two
source: Ownership Map v1 api rows POST /cases/{caseId}/instructions, GET /partner/instructions, POST /partner/instructions/{instructionId}/accept and POST /partner/instructions/{instructionId}/results with owner S9; Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 19 IN, OUT and notes; Temporal and Drools Design Text Extract v1 slides 13, 14 and 27
description: The Ownership Map publishes a partner REST surface for instructions with owner S9, while Architecture v5 slide 19 OUT names TMP Partner: issueInstruction as a Temporal call of rwb-asset and the Temporal and Drools Design model requires the cross-service call of a stage to be an activity on the owner's queue with its answer recorded in history. Both cannot be the call this step makes, no source says which one it is, and the contract has to declare one call type and state what the other surface is.
evidence: Ownership Map v1 api rows POST /cases/{caseId}/instructions, GET /partner/instructions, POST /partner/instructions/{instructionId}/accept and POST /partner/instructions/{instructionId}/results with owner S9; Architecture v5 slide 19 OUT line TMP Partner: issueInstruction (auction vendor); Architecture v5 slide 19 notes tag TMP = Temporal activity or child workflow on the owner's task queue; Temporal and Drools Design v1 slide 13 note each stage is a child workflow started on the owner's queue and slide 27 activity code calls partners
proposed: Declare the Temporal activity as the call this service makes, record the partner REST path as the partner gateway surface rwb-partner uses, and add a drift test that fails a build which declares the partner path on rwb-asset

title: The buy-back step has no operation of its own and the consumed rows have no published operation names
source: Legacy RWB-E4-032 Endpoints table; Ownership Map v1 API rows; TSD S5 Assets and auction v2 T-A.1; Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 19 and 41; API Specification v4
description: The legacy story names two endpoints, GET /api/recovery/v1/assets/{assetId} and POST /api/recovery/v1/assets/{assetId}/listings. Neither opens a buy-back: the first is the asset read moved to the target base, the second is the pricing story's listing operation, and the inventory adds POST /assets/{assetId}/valuations, which is rwb-valuation's under ASM-A6-api-6. No source names an operation that opens a buy-back, and no source publishes the operation name or identifier of the rwb-deviation raise, of the rwb-decision approval child workflow or of the rwb-case case-move answer.
evidence: Legacy Endpoints: GET /api/recovery/v1/assets/{assetId} (Asset and disposal R); POST /api/recovery/v1/assets/{assetId}/listings (Asset and disposal C). Ownership Map: POST /cases/{caseId}/deviations owner S8; GET /assets and POST /assets/{assetId}/listings owner S5; POST /assets/{assetId}/valuations owner S1 (ASM-A6-api-6). Architecture v5 slide 19 OUT: Decision: child: approval.
owner_role: Tech lead of rwb-asset with the owners of rwb-case and rwb-deviation
proposed: Declare the two asset reads as provided, the four consumed rows with the placeholder and a faked answer, and the buy-back as an element of the Asset answer rather than an operation; confirm each consumed name with its owner before the baseline is tagged.

title: Which table and column hold the buy-back terms and the template price is not settled and the template price has no field identifier
source: TSD S5 Assets and auction v2 T3.1; Ownership Map v1 table rows; Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 R-DIS-24 and R-DIS-61; FSD S5 Assets and auction v3 A2.23
description: The rules say the buy-back terms are agreed and completed at the template price, but no source gives the price a field identifier or names the table that holds it. listing carries start_price, floor_price and status (DF-SAL-004, DF-SAL-005, DF-SAL-008) and asset_sale carries contract_date, sale_date and sale_price (DF-SAL-012 to DF-SAL-014); the template itself is the template table, which the Ownership Map gives to P6 rwb-comms, and no TSD gives a read operation for it. Whether the template price sits on the listing, on the sale terms or in a third table is therefore unstated.
evidence: TSD S5 T3.1: listing DF-SAL-001 to DF-SAL-008; asset_sale DF-SAL-009 to DF-SAL-019. Ownership Map: template owner P6 (Architecture v5 slide 41, rwb-comms owns notices, templates, merge fields). Business Rules v4 R-DIS-24 Agree the buy-back terms at the template price; R-DIS-61 Complete the buy-back at the governed template price.
owner_role: Tech lead of rwb-asset with the owner of rwb-comms and the data steward
proposed: Write the terms on asset_sale with listing_id pointing at the buy-back listing and sale_price taken from the template price reference with its template version; add no table and no column and leave the price field and its read operation to P6.

title: The approval the limit requires has no limit value in any source and no published approval shape
source: Legacy RWB-E4-032 AC1; FSD S5 Assets and auction v3 A2.23.3.1; Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 R-DIS-24; Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 19 and 41; Ownership Map v1 table rows
description: The legacy story, the FSD rule VR-S5-023-1 and R-DIS-24 all require the approval the limit requires, and none of them gives the limit or says who holds it. The ownership map gives approval to P7 rwb-decision and the delegated-authority table to P4 rwb-access, the approval is the kit's approval child workflow on rwb-decision, and neither its element names nor its answered and refused shapes are published in the sources read for this story.
evidence: Legacy AC1: with the approval the limit requires. FSD A2.23.3.1: VR-S5-023-1 Floor price below the approver's limit and MSG-S5-001 with the {pct} and {limit} placeholders. Ownership Map: approval owner P7; Architecture v5 slide 41 rwb-access owns the DoA table. Architecture v5 slide 19 OUT: Decision: child: approval.
owner_role: Owner of rwb-decision with the owner of rwb-access
proposed: Take the approval as the kit's approval child workflow on rwb-decision and read the limit from the delegated-authority rows of rwb-access at their version; write no limit value in code, in a test or in a fixture.

title: The buy-back channel and the buy-back listing status have no value in the closed lists
source: TSD S5 Assets and auction v2 T3.2; FSD S5 Assets and auction v3 A2.23.3.2; legacy RWB-E4-032 Data
description: The buy-back is opened as a listing of the asset, and every listing row carries sale_channel and status, both closed lists. LOV-SALE-CHANNEL offers DUTCH_AUCTION, BROKER, DIRECT, LED_AUCTION and RAMC and LOV-LISTING offers DRAFT, LIVE, UNDER_OFFER, SOLD and WITHDRAWN; neither carries a buy-back value and no source says which value an approved buy-back writes or whether the holding status of the asset moves.
evidence: TSD S5 T3.2: LOV-SALE-CHANNEL = DUTCH_AUCTION, BROKER, DIRECT, LED_AUCTION, RAMC; LOV-LISTING = DRAFT, LIVE, UNDER_OFFER, SOLD, WITHDRAWN; LOV-HOLDING = HELD, LISTED, UNDER_OFFER, SOLD, TRANSFERRED, RENTED. TSD S5 T3.1 listing DF-SAL-003 sale_channel and DF-SAL-008 status are required.
owner_role: Owner of the reference data with the tech lead of rwb-asset
proposed: Read both lists as reference data at their version and carry the value as a placeholder until the reference-data owner publishes a buy-back entry; add no list value in code and leave the asset holding status unchanged in this step.

title: Legacy AC1 gives no from state while the buy-back rule starts at ROUTE_WITH_APPROVER and the asset is held
source: Legacy RWB-E4-032 AC1; Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 R-DIS-19, R-DIS-20, R-DIS-24; TSD S5 Assets and auction v2 T4
description: AC1 states only that the data and the rule version are in place, and it names no case state. The rule that agrees the buy-back terms, R-DIS-24, runs from ROUTE_WITH_APPROVER, which the disposal machine reaches from ASSET_HELD through R-DIS-19 and R-DIS-20, while the legacy criterion and the FSD describe the asset as held when the buy-back is opened. The state the step sees and the state the rule starts from are therefore described differently.
evidence: Legacy AC1: Given the data and the rule version this feature needs are in place. Business Rules v4: R-DIS-19 from ASSET_HELD to ROUTE_RECOMMENDED; R-DIS-20 from ROUTE_RECOMMENDED to ROUTE_WITH_APPROVER; R-DIS-24 from ROUTE_WITH_APPROVER on ROUTE_APPROVED with route = buy_back and second_signature given to ROUTE_APPROVED_BUYBACK.
owner_role: Owner of rwb-decision with the owner of rwb-case
proposed: Read the case state and the route on the rwb-case contract, require ROUTE_WITH_APPROVER with the buy-back route for R-DIS-24, and let the case-move answer carry ROUTE_APPROVED_BUYBACK; state in the tests that the asset is held while the route is with the approver.

title: The FSD lists the customer as an also-user of the feature and the rights matrix has no customer role
source: FSD S5 Assets and auction v3 A2.23.3.3; TSD S5 Assets and auction v2 T6.1; Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 20
description: The FSD gives the feature the sale officer as primary user and Head of NPA and Customer (borrower) as also-users. TSD S5 T6.1, which is the rights matrix of the module, has no customer or borrower role, and Architecture v5 slide 20 states that partners and customers do not use gateway-bff and reach the bank through the partner gateway to rwb-partner. The role the borrower acts under, and whether the former owner sees or signs the buy-back of the Workbench at all, is therefore not settled.
evidence: FSD A2.23.3.3: Sale officer, Primary; Head of NPA, Customer (borrower), Also uses. TSD S5 T6.1 lists 30 roles, none of them a customer or borrower. Architecture v5 slide 20: Partners do not use it: partner gateway to rwb-partner.
owner_role: Owner of rwb-access with the sales business owner
proposed: Represent the former owner by the sale officer acting on the case and carry the former owner as a party key the owner's contract answers; add no customer role, no customer screen and no external edge in this story.

title: The split plan carries no requirement id for this slice
source: Split plan requirement rows for this key; Business Requirements Program v4 REQ-S5-010; FSD S5 Assets and auction v3 requirements served
description: The plan row for this story carries an empty requirement list, while the program and the FSD give the slice REQ-S5-010, that a transfer to the asset management company, a buy-back and a rental each follow a recorded approval. The trace therefore rests on the module requirement and not on a plan row.
evidence: Business Requirements Program v4: REQ-S5-010 A transfer to the asset management company, a buy-back and a rental each follow a recorded approval, Must, Head of NPA, E4. FSD S5 requirements served repeats the same row. The plan requirement list for RWB-S5-E4032-APP and RWB-S5-E4032-CON is empty.
owner_role: Traceability manager with the business analyst
proposed: Trace both stories to REQ-S5-010 in place of a plan requirement row and let the register carry the absence.

title: No published surface exists for the buy-back step so the baseline declares it as an element and the consumed rows as placeholders
source: Legacy RWB-E4-032 Endpoints table; Ownership Map v1 API rows; TSD S5 Assets and auction v2 T-A.1 and T3.2; Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 19 and 41
description: The contract baseline has to declare the buy-back surface, and no source gives one: there is no operation that opens a buy-back, no operation name for the rwb-case case-move answer, the rwb-deviation raise or the rwb-decision approval, and no value in LOV-SALE-CHANNEL or LOV-LISTING for a buy-back. The only operations the sources give the service are the two asset reads, the listing and the auction rounds, and the valuations that belong to rwb-valuation under ASM-A6-api-6.
evidence: Ownership Map: GET /assets, GET /assets/{assetId}, POST /assets/{assetId}/listings and POST /listings/{listingId}/rounds owner S5; POST /assets/{assetId}/valuations owner S1 (ASM-A6-api-6); POST /cases/{caseId}/deviations owner S8. TSD S5 T-A.1 lists API-S5-001 to API-S5-005 only. TSD S5 T3.2 lists LOV-SALE-CHANNEL and LOV-LISTING without a buy-back value.
proposed: Declare the two asset reads as provided, the buy-back as an element of the Asset answer and as rows of listing and asset_sale, and the four consumed rows with the placeholder; add no operation, no list value and no property of another owner.

title: The approval answer and the template price element are not published and their fakes are derived
source: Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 19 OUT; Ownership Map v1 table rows; TSD S5 Assets and auction v2 T3.1; Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 R-DIS-24
